learningObjective: Create public IP addresses and prefixes, choose the SKU, assignment, tier and zone settings, and attach them to resources.
engineer: SKU: Standard is the only choice for new public IPs (Basic was retired on 30 September 2025).
Standard public IPs: always static; closed to incoming traffic until an NSG allows it (secure by default); support availability zones.
Zone options: zone-redundant, survives a zone failure; zonal, pinned to one zone; no zone. You can't change this after creation.
Tier: Regional, the normal one; Global, used with the cross-region load balancer.
Routing preference: Microsoft network, the default, where traffic stays on Microsoft's network as long as possible; Internet, cheaper, where traffic uses internet providers' networks.
Public IP prefix: reserves a block of static addresses next to each other (for example a /28), so partners can allow-list one range.
Cost: you pay for every public IP per hour, attached or not.

Attaching: attach or detach a public IP on a network card's (NIC's) IP configuration. A VM can have one public IP per IP configuration. If the VM only needs to reach the internet (outbound), use a NAT gateway instead.

example.title: Giving a partner fixed addresses
body: A partner must allow-list Contoso's outgoing addresses. Contoso creates a /30 public IP prefix and gives its addresses to a NAT gateway. Now all outgoing traffic uses four known IPs.

architectureDecisions: Keep public IPs off VMs: use Bastion for admin, and a load balancer or Application Gateway for apps.
Fixed ranges for partners: use a public IP prefix.

misconceptions.myth: Public IPs are free when they're not attached.
misconceptions.reality: No. Public IPv4 addresses are billed every hour.

misconceptions.myth: A Standard public IP is open to the internet.
misconceptions.reality: No. Incoming traffic is blocked until an NSG allows it.

comparisons.difference: Lets a whole subnet reach the internet using fixed public IPs. Outbound only: nothing can come in.
A fixed public IPv4 address you attach to an instance or NAT gateway.

troubleshooting.symptom: A VM with a Standard public IP can't be reached.
troubleshooting.cause: Standard IPs block incoming traffic by default.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an NSG rule that allows the port.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't attach the public IP to a Standard load balancer.
The public IP changed after the VM was deallocated.
troubleshooting.cause: It was a dynamic IP (old Basic SKU).

configuration.limits: A public IP quota per region (the default depends on the subscription)
Zone and SKU can't be changed after creation
configuration.permissions: Network Contributor on the resource group
